subject: Responsibility titles now match earned levels
description: Responsibility Pillar titles now start at level 2 instead of level 1. The earned identities section only shows titles a child has actually unlocked, so early XP in other pillars no longer clutters the list.

subject: Chore celebrations now start right away
description: The chore completion celebration now appears right away, stays visible long enough to read, includes a dismiss button, shows Responsibility Pillar progress when XP is awarded, and calls out New Skill bonuses with a special headline.

subject: Chore completions now show Responsibility progress
description: When a completed chore adds Responsibility XP, the Done celebration now shows the pillar, level, XP gain, and progress toward the next title so kids can see exactly how their work helped them grow.

subject: Kiosk Mode can include parents too
description: Kiosk Mode now lets families include parent profiles in the shared-tablet roster, so parents with their own chores can use the same focused checklist while parent controls stay locked until Kiosk Mode is exited.

subject: Dashboard avatars now open Responsibility Progress
description: The dashboard chore list now lets you tap a child's avatar to open their Responsibility Progress without leaving the page, replacing the separate Family Growth card. The approval card's caught-up message also keeps its close button neatly inline on mobile.

subject: Routines now reveal one step at a time, everywhere
description: Routine chores are meant to surface a single next step instead of dumping every step into the list at once. The mobile app now collapses routine steps the same way the web dashboard does, so your child only sees the step they're on. Google Tasks sync was also creating every routine step as a separate task all at once — it now pushes only the current step, then the next one appears after each step is finished, keeping your Google Tasks list tidy.

subject: Responsibility titles now show up across the whole app
description: The identities your kids earn no longer live only on the Pillars page. Player dashboards now feature a "Your Journey" card showing the title they hold and how close they are to the next one, with one tap to the full Pillars view. Profiles lead with each child's earned titles, and the profile/kiosk switcher shows title chips under each name so picking a profile feels like choosing a character. Parents get a new "Family Growth" section on the dashboard summarizing every child's top title at a glance, and unlocking a new title now posts a distinct, celebratory card in the family activity feed that stays in your history.

subject: Responsibility Pillars now grant titles your kids grow into
description: Each Responsibility Pillar now turns progress into an identity instead of just a number. As children build XP, their level unlocks titles like Helper → Housekeeper → Chore Master for Home Care, with a matching ladder of seven titles for every pillar. The Responsibility Progress card leads with each child's current title, the next title, and how close they are to it, plus a strip of the identities they've already earned. When a chore completion grows a pillar, kids see a quick celebration showing their title and progress bar climbing — and when they reach a brand-new title, it's marked with confetti and announced in the family activity feed so parents can celebrate the moment too.

subject: Weekly highlights email now invites you to link Athena
description: The weekly family highlights email features a new callout for the Athena Learning Companion. Families who haven't connected yet get a one-tap link to pair their account, with a reminder of what Athena unlocks: smarter, more personalized chore suggestions for each child, and the ability for kids to ask Athena how many coins they have and which chore to work on next. Once you're connected, the callout disappears so the recap stays focused on your week.

subject: New Approval Inbox makes reviewing finished chores effortless
description: Parents now have one obvious place to celebrate and approve completed chores. A new card at the top of your dashboard shows how many chores are waiting, who finished them, and lets you approve a whole day's worth in a couple of taps. The dedicated Approval Inbox groups chores by child, shows each chore's coins, pillar, and completion time, and walks you through awarding coins for See & Do chores so nothing is approved at zero by mistake. A live count in the navigation means you'll never have to hunt for approvals again.

subject: Mobile app no longer freezes when it can't reach the server
description: If the mobile app can't connect to Family Chores — for example on a weak or dropped network — it now shows a clear "Can't reach the server" message with a Try Again button instead of getting stuck on "Checking session…" or freezing during Google sign-in. Requests now time out gracefully rather than hanging indefinitely.

subject: Smoother Kiosk Mode on mobile
description: Completing your last chore in Kiosk Mode on the mobile app no longer shows a spurious error when tapped quickly, and the "All done!" celebration now plays once instead of repeating. The shared-tablet screen also refreshes quietly in the background instead of flashing a loading spinner every few seconds.

subject: Athena now “thinks” before sharing chore ideas
description: While Athena prepares suggestions, you'll see a delightful new moment instead of a loading spinner: Athena's avatar gently glows and “thinks” about your family's progress, with encouraging messages that build as she works. When she's ready she celebrates and reveals her ideas one at a time, each with a friendly reason. If she can't find something new, or is briefly unavailable, she says so kindly and falls back to her saved suggestions. The whole experience respects reduced-motion settings and works on web and mobile.

subject: Smarter chore ideas powered by Athena
description: When your family connects the Athena learning companion, the suggested "ghost" chores that appear when there's nothing left to do are now AI-personalized — age-aware, mindful of what's already been done, and each with a short reason, difficulty, and time estimate. If Athena isn't connected or is unavailable, the familiar built-in suggestions still appear. Parents can also set a child's birth year on their profile so suggestions fit their age, and every suggestion still needs a parent's OK before it becomes a real, paid chore.

subject: Bug & feature requests work for parents on shared profiles
description: Submitting and viewing your bug reports and feature requests no longer fails with a permissions error when you've switched into a child's profile or are using Kiosk Mode. Requests are now tied to your signed-in parent account, and the Requests tab is shown only on admin profiles.

subject: Recurring routines no longer restart the same day
description: Completing a recurring routine that was due on an earlier day no longer immediately spawns another occurrence due today. The next occurrence is now scheduled from the completion date — so a daily routine always waits until tomorrow — matching how recurring chores already behave.

subject: Streamlined add/edit chore form
description: The add/edit chore form now pairs related fields side by side on wider screens — Assignee with Coin Value, Due Date with Recurrence, Responsibility Pillar with Categories, and Require Parent Approval with New Skill Bonus — for a more compact layout. The separate Additional Details field has been removed.

subject: Evening chores now default to today
description: Creating a chore in the evening no longer defaults its due date to tomorrow. The default due date now follows your local calendar day instead of UTC, so a chore added after 8 PM is correctly due today.

subject: Filter chores by upcoming
description: The Chores page has a new "Upcoming" filter that shows active chores and routines scheduled to start in the future (due tomorrow or later). It's an easy way to find a chore that doesn't begin until a later date — handy when you want to move it up to today.

subject: Achievements count shared chores
description: Completing a chore that's shared with the whole family or assigned to more than one person now counts toward your achievements. Streaks, "chores in a day/week", category explorer, teamwork, and Bounce Back progress for every assignee on the chore — previously these only tracked chores assigned to a single person.

subject: Query player chores over the API
description: The public API has a new read-only endpoint, GET /api/v1/players/{playerId}/chores, so connected assistants like Athena can answer questions such as "What chores did I complete last week?", "What's still left to do today?", "What chores will I have tomorrow?", and "What Vivacity chores do I have?". Results can be filtered by date range, completion status, and category, and future occurrences of recurring chores are projected for upcoming windows. It uses the existing read:chores scope.

subject: Developer API shows active tokens
description: The Developer API panel now loads active API tokens and their recent activity, keeps today's usage chart in sync with current requests, and hides token prefixes and raw endpoint paths from token cards.

subject: Mobile sign-in header fit
description: The logged-out mobile header now keeps the Google sign-in button beside the Family Chores brand, so the header no longer grows over the homepage hero.

subject: Refreshed Developer API panel
description: The Developer API section in your profile has a cleaner, easier-to-read design. Creating a token now happens in a focused dialog, your tokens and usage history fill the full width of the page, scopes are selectable pills, each token shows a live daily-usage meter and its scopes at a glance, and there's a 7-day usage chart plus a color-coded audit trail of recent API calls.

subject: Custom recurrence picker
description: Parents can now open a dedicated Custom recurrence picker when setting chores or assigning routines, including weekly schedules like every Tuesday, weekdays, or every other Tuesday.

subject: Save See and Do coins before approval
description: Parents can now save coins on a See and Do chore before approval, see the saved amount in the app, and approve the chore later without being asked to enter the coins again.

subject: Responsibility Pillars, Routines, and Responsibility XP
description: Family Chores now helps kids build real life skills, not just check off tasks. Build reusable Routines — like Clean Room or Morning Routine — from a sequence of smaller chores, then assign them straight from the dashboard's new + Add menu with due dates and repeats. Each routine step appears in the chore list like a normal chore (approvals, New Skill Bonus, and Kiosk Mode included), with a routine badge you can tap to see overall progress, and finishing the last step pays a routine completion bonus. Tag chores and routines with one of five Responsibility Pillars — Home Care, Self Care, Organization, Family Contribution, and Life Skills — and kids earn Responsibility XP and pillar levels as they grow, all visible on the profile's Responsibility Progress card.

subject: New Skill Bonus for first-time chores
description: Kids now earn a one-time +5 coin New Skill Bonus the first time they ever complete a chore — including the first time they tackle a recurring chore. The dashboard shows a sparkly "New Skill +5" badge on chores a child hasn't done before, and recurring chores get a calendar icon you can tap to reveal how often they repeat.

subject: Family Kiosk Mode for shared tablets
description: Open Kiosk Mode from the profile menu to turn any family tablet into a simple, focused chore checklist. Pick a player, complete their chores, and switch players or exit with your PIN. Kiosk Mode always stays player-level, so parent, admin, and support controls are never exposed on the shared device.

subject: Reorder chores again after sorting
description: The dashboard sort menu now includes a Manual order option, so you can clear an active sort and go back to dragging or moving chores to set their priority. Disabled move controls now explain why they're unavailable.

subject: Report bugs, request features, ask questions, and share feedback
description: You can now tell us what you think right from the app. Report a bug, request a feature, ask a question, or share general feedback — set how important it is, and choose whether we can follow up and notify you when the status changes. We'll keep you posted as your request moves from planned to released.

subject: Terms acceptance no longer restarts onboarding
description: Accepting the latest Terms & Conditions now only records your consent — families that already have children go straight to the dashboard instead of being sent back through new-family setup. This prevents duplicate child profiles from being created.

subject: Dashboard chore visibility
description: Dashboard chores now load consistently for families with longer chore histories while keeping future-dated chores out of the current list.

subject: Dashboard chore filters
description: The Chores dashboard now has a quick filter menu for category, chore type, and due date, with active filters shown above the list and saved after refreshing the page.

subject: Richer family privacy controls
description: Family Privacy now groups legal and consent actions together, opens your accepted Terms and Privacy documents in dialogs, includes a dedicated consent history page, and streamlines consent and family data actions.

subject: Guided onboarding for new families
description: New parents now experience a focused step-by-step setup: welcome, family naming, privacy & consent, adding a first child, and creating a first chore — all before reaching the dashboard. Existing families are not affected.

subject: Shared category assignments
description: Categories can now be assigned to multiple family members, making shared chore labels easier to reuse.

subject: Friendly color names
description: Store theme swatches and family category color pickers now use playful color names instead of raw hex codes.

subject: What's New badges
description: Red badges now show what's new since you last looked — new chores, store items, quests, achievements, and changelog updates — with a What's New card on your dashboard. Opening a section clears its badge, and counts respect each profile's role and access.

subject: Sticky chore defaults
description: New chore dialogs now remember your last coin value and category selections so repeated chore setup is faster.

subject: Weekly Family Highlights Email
description: Parents can receive a weekly summary of completed chores, coins earned, rewards, quests, achievements, and helpful family tips.

subject: Family Activity Feed
description: Families can now see recent chores, rewards, achievements, quests, and other progress in one cheerful dashboard feed. The signed-in dashboard keeps your familiar Chores view front and center, with a new Feed tab a tap away.

subject: Store purchase confirmation
description: Purchasing an item in the Store now shows a confirmation dialog with the item image, a message telling you where it was added (Inventory, Unclaimed Family Awards, or Profile), and quick actions to equip it, claim it, or jump to the relevant section.

subject: Richer profile overview
description: Profile pages now show pending family awards and owned item summaries so kids can see rewards and inventory in one place.

subject: Smart Ghost Chores
description: When a player runs out of chores, the dashboard now suggests safe, age-appropriate "Suggested Chore" ideas. Add one with a tap or dismiss it to see another, and hover a suggestion to learn why it was picked. Suggestions are clearly marked and never affect coins, stats, or streaks until they're added. Available on web and mobile.

subject: Community Award Library
description: Parents can submit Family Awards for review, browse approved community ideas from the Family Awards tab, vote on favorites, and copy them into their own family. The library is also available on mobile.

subject: Public requested changes
description: The change log now includes requested changes that support has chosen to publish, with public statuses and upvotes for signed-in users.

subject: Better support request tracking
description: Support operators can now review bug reports and feature requests, update their status, and track request history in the support console.

subject: Report bugs and request features
description: You can now report a bug or request a feature right from the profile menu. Add a subject and description (and a severity for bugs) and send it our way. Available on web and mobile.

subject: A friendlier empty dashboard
description: When there are no open chores, the dashboard now shows a clear, friendly message with an icon and a quick action to add a chore, instead of a single line of text.

subject: Friendlier first steps
description: Parents whose family has no kids yet now see a gentle prompt to add their first family member, and brand-new players get a quick welcome explaining how to earn and spend coins. Both can be dismissed.

subject: First-time Google sign-in
description: Fixed an error that could stop brand-new accounts from finishing their first Google sign-in and creating their family.

subject: A head start for new families
description: New families now begin with a guided getting-started checklist, example categories, and a starter reward so your dashboard is ready to use right away. Complete the steps to set up your family, then edit or remove anything to make it your own.

subject: Group chore approval payouts
description: Fixed group chore approval so parents can exclude assignees and the remaining coins re-split automatically before approval.

subject: Faster chore editing
description: The add chore form now keeps the most-used fields up front, remembers additional options, and defaults the assignee from your dashboard filter.

subject: Dashboard chore deletion
description: Removed the extra delete animation from dashboard chore cards so chores disappear more cleanly.

subject: Notification badge clearing
description: Fixed an issue where the unseen notification count could stay visible after a player viewed unseen notifications.

subject: Language support
description: Users can now choose their preferred language, parents can update language settings for family members, and quests can support localized content.

subject: Newly added chores on dashboard
description: Fixed an issue where some newly added chores did not appear on the dashboard or all chores table right away.
